2 HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioners have sought for issuance of writ of certiorari quashing a portion of the order dated 04.04.2022 and an endorsement dated 21.04.2022 insofar as the condition requiring the petitioners to get rectification of the survey number in the sale deed for the purposes of getting compensation as at Annexures- A and B.
The petitioners have also sought for direction to the respondents to allot them developed eligible sites for their 2 acre of land as compensation as per the applicable Scheme.

2. The petitioners submit that they are the owners of land in Survey No.51/1A of Kommaghatta village, Kengeri Hobli, Bangalore South Taluk, which was notified NC: 2023:KHC:21154 for formation of a layout called "Nadaprabhu Kempegowda Layout".
It is submitted that the petitioners are the legal heirs of one Munishamappa who had purchased 1 acre in Sy.No.51 through a sale deed dated 08.06.1959.
Further, it is stated that another extent of 2 acre of land in Sy.No.51 was purchased on 04.11.1961.
It is submitted that in the sale deed dated 04.11.1961, the survey number was wrongly mentioned as '51/2' instead of "51/1" and the old survey number corresponds to new No.51/1A.
It is submitted that the boundaries clearly reveal the identity of the land as land in Sy.No.51/1A.

It is submitted that out of the total extent of 3 acres, the legal heirs of Munishamappa have sold 1 acre to third persons and accordingly the petitioners restrict their claim, as absolute owners, to an extent of 2 acres in Sy.No.51, now Survey No.51/1A.

The petitioners submit that in the light of the mistake in the sale deed, wherein the sale deed mentioned the survey number as '51/2',
the compensation has not been settled to the petitioners.
Further, attention is drawn to the order passed in W.P.No.42151/2019 disposed of on 16.04.2021.

During the pendency of the said writ petition, an interim direction was issued on 26.02.2021 which reads as follows:
"Learned counsel for the respondents submits that in light of certain allegations made by the petitioners the disbursal of compensation as regards Sy.No.51/1A has been kept in abeyance.

2. It is further submitted that in light of the allegations as made by the petitioners, an enquiry is being held as regards to the decision to disburse compensation in terms of agreement under Section 29(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

3. Further in light of the dispute with respect to identity of survey number,
respondent No.2 to also make out a report after enquiry as to whether Sy.No.51/1A is the same as Sy.No.51/2 in which petitioners' claim title.

sentences.text: The petitioners to appear before the respondent No.2 without any further notice on 16.03.2021.

Further consideration is deferred till the conclusion of the enquiry."
4.

The Court while disposing of W.P.No.42151/2019 has also noticed that an enquiry was conducted by the respondent - Special Task Force and enquiry report was also submitted before the Court and the Court at Paragraphs - 4 and 5 in W.P.No.42151/2019 has observed as follows:
"4. Pursuant to the aforesaid orders, respondent No.2 BDA has conducted an enquiry and filed a memo of even date enclosing a report of the Special Task Force of the BDA.
In the said report, the BDA has specifically stated that the respondent No.2-BDA would address the grievance of the petitioners in relation to compensation payable in favour of the petitioners.
The said memo and report are placed on record.

In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, I deem it just and appropriate to dispose of this petition directing the respondent No.2 - BDA to take necessary steps with regard to payment of compensation by way of cash/allotment of developed land in lieu of the compensation in favour of the petitioners in terms of the aforesaid report dated 06.04.2021 within a period of three months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order."
5.

It is noticed that in terms of the directions in W.P. No.42151/2019, the Bangalore Development Authority was directed to take necessary steps with regard to payment of compensation by way of cash/allotment of developed land in lieu of compensation in favour of the petitioners in terms of the Report dated 06.04.2021 within a period of three months.

6. It is also noticed that a Review Petition in R.P. No.629/2022 came to be filed seeking for review of the order passed in W.P.No.42151/2019 and the said Review NC: 2023:KHC:21154 Petition was filed after endorsement was issued at Annexure-B dated 21.04.2022 which endorsement was issued during the pendency of the contempt proceedings initiated by the petitioners in CCC No.203/2022.
7.

A careful perusal of the said Review Petition would reveal that there is no interference with the operative directions issued in W.P.No.42151/2019 except reserving liberty to the petitioners to challenge the order and the endorsement dated 04.04.2022 and 21.04.2022 respectively.
8. Perused the report which is submitted along with a memo in W.P.No.42151/2019.

The relevant observations made are extracted below:

10. The respondents stand by the contents of the Report.
Further, the direction in W.P.No.42151/2019 was to disburse compensation in terms of the Report.

Accordingly, what now requires to be done is to treat the entitlement of the petitioners as being entitlement to compensation with respect to Sy.No.51/1A, which would be in terms of the finding of the Report pursuant to the direction in W.P.No.42151/2019.

11. A perusal of the operative portion of the order dated 04.04.2022 and the endorsement dated 21.04.2022 would only reveal that they are issued on the premise that the petitioners' entitlement is with respect to Survey No.51/1A though in the sale deed dated 04.11.1961, the survey number is wrongly mentioned as '51/2'.

However this issue relating to identity is settled by the direction issued Smt. Narasamma vs Bangalore Development Authority on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/28085752/
5 in W.P.No.42151/2019 which direction has not been altered even in the Review Petition and has attained finality.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the petition stands disposed off.
The order dated 04.04.2022 and the endorsement dated - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC:21154 21.04.2022 at Annexures-A and B are set aside insofar as the direction for rectification of the revenue records.

13. The question of rectification of revenue records may not arise at this stage as the land has been acquired and compensation deposited and also in the light of the observations made in the previous round of litigation in W.P.No.42151/2019 wherein the identity being sought to be ascertained by way of enquiry, the said enquiry has been completed holding that the survey number mentioned in the sale deed ought to be read as '51/2' which now is 51/1A.
14.

The respondents are directed to adhere to the directions issued in W.P.No.42151/2019.
15.

The claim of the petitioners for compensation by way of allotment of developed eligible sites to be taken note of in terms of the preamble to the Notification under Sections 17(1) and (3) of the Bangalore Development - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC:21154 Authority Act, 1976 as annexed at Annexure - C and in terms of the eligibility of the petitioners for developed eligible sites for their 2 acre of land as compensation as per the applicable Scheme.
